label: April 8, 2025
changes_html:
About This Vintage

This is a historical reconstruction of The Budget Lab's "State of U.S. Tariffs: Week of April 7, 2025" report, restructured to match the current interactive's data format. This report captured tariff policy shortly after the April 2 "Liberation Day" reciprocal tariff announcement and China's retaliatory tariff increase to 34%, effective April 10.

Baseline

This section presents projected effects as of April 8, 2025, reflecting all 2025 tariffs and foreign retaliation implemented through the week of April 7. Estimated impacts are measured against a January 2025 tariff-policy baseline.

spec.title: US Average Effective Tariff Rate Since 1790
spec.subtitle: Customs duty revenue as a percentage of goods imports.
spec.source: Historical Statistics of the United States Ea424-434, Monthly Treasury Statement, Bureau of Economic Analysis, The Budget Lab analysis.

figures.body_html: The US average effective tariff rate since 1790, with the current (April 8, 2025) average effective rate shown for reference. This figure is not part of the current interactive's standard figure set and is included here as an extra, since it was published in this release.
figures.note: No direct analogue in the reference (2025-10-30) vintage structure; included as an additional figure.

spec.title: Long-Run Commodity Price Effects, Overall / Domestic / Imported
spec.subtitle: Percent change to price level. Through week of April 7.
spec.source: GTAP v7 [Corong et al (2017)], The Budget Lab analysis.
spec.notes: "nec" = "Not elsewhere classified." Only long-run (post-substitution) values were published in this release. The "basis" field splits each commodity into its overall, domestic-price, and imported-price change, as delineated in the source workbook.

figures.body_html: Long-run overall, domestic, and imported price effects for the commodities with the largest projected changes, as of the week of April 7, 2025. No short-run (pre-substitution) commodity-level breakdown was published in this release.

spec.title: Household Cost of Tariffs by Income Decile
spec.subtitle: Tariff burden by household income decile, post-substitution. Through week of April 7.
spec.source: GTAP v7, Census, BLS, BEA, The Budget Lab analysis.
spec.notes: Decile 1 values were not published in this release.

figures.body_html: The tariff burden by household income decile, as a share of after-tax income and in 2024 dollars per household. Values are negative by convention. Decile 1 was not published in this release.

spec.title: Effect on Real GDP over Time
spec.subtitle: Percent change in the level of real GDP versus baseline.
spec.source: S&P Global, GTAP v7, GTAP RD, The Budget Lab analysis.

figures.body_html: The projected path of real GDP relative to a no-new-tariffs baseline, by quarter.

spec.title: Long-Run Change in Real GDP by Trading Partner
spec.subtitle: Percent change in the level of real GDP versus baseline.
spec.source: GTAP v7 [Corong et al (2017)], The Budget Lab analysis.
spec.notes: FTROW = countries with a comprehensive free trade agreement with the US. ROW = all other countries. Only country-level effects were published in this release; no sector-level breakdown is available for this vintage.

figures.body_html: The long-run change in real GDP, by trading partner. No sector-level breakdown was published in this release.
